questions.knowledgeNote: f'(a) = lim(h->0)[f(a+h)-f(a)]/h. For x + sqrt(x) rationalise the surd: the quotient is 1 + 1/[sqrt(x+h)+sqrt(x)] -> 1 + 1/(2 sqrt x).
questions.question: Q1. Define differential coefficient of a function at a given point. Find, from first principles, the derivative of x + sqrt(x) with respect to x. (T.U. 2051)
questions.solution: Definition. The differential coefficient (derivative) of f at the point x = a is f'(a) = lim(h->0) [f(a+h) - f(a)]/h, when this limit exists; it is the instantaneous rate of change of f at a and, geometrically, the slope of the tangent to y = f(x) at (a, f(a)). Step 1 (difference quotient). With f(x) = x + sqrt(x): [f(x+h) - f(x)]/h = {h + [sqrt(x+h) - sqrt(x)]}/h = 1 + [sqrt(x+h) - sqrt(x)]/h. Step 2 (rationalise the surd). sqrt(x+h) - sqrt(x) = [(x+h) - x]/[sqrt(x+h) + sqrt(x)] = h/[sqrt(x+h) + sqrt(x)], so the quotient = 1 + 1/[sqrt(x+h) + sqrt(x)]. Step 3 (h -> 0). sqrt(x+h) -> sqrt(x), giving 1 + 1/(2 sqrt(x)). Boxed d/dx [x + sqrt(x)] = 1 + 1/(2 sqrt(x)), x > 0 (printed key p533: 1 + 1/(2 sqrt(x))).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q1; book p532-534 = PDF p559-561; key book p533-534

questions.knowledgeNote: sin(x+h) - sin x = 2 cos(x + h/2) sin(h/2); sin u/u -> 1 gives cos x. Physical readings: velocity, acceleration, general instantaneous rate.
questions.question: Q2. Define the differential coefficient of a function at a given point. What are its physical meanings? Find from definition the differential coefficient of sin x with respect to x. (T.U. 2052)
questions.solution: Definition. f'(a) = lim(h->0) [f(a+h) - f(a)]/h is the differential coefficient of f at x = a, the limit of the average rate of change over a shrinking interval [a, a+h]. Physical meanings. (i) If s = f(t) is the distance moved in time t, then f'(t) is the instantaneous velocity. (ii) If v = f(t) is velocity, then f'(t) is the instantaneous acceleration. (iii) In general f'(a) is the instantaneous rate of change of f with respect to x at x = a (rate of cooling, rate of growth, marginal cost, ...). Derivative of sin x. [sin(x+h) - sin x]/h = [2 cos(x + h/2) sin(h/2)]/h (sum-to-product) = cos(x + h/2) * [sin(h/2)/(h/2)]. As h -> 0, sin(h/2)/(h/2) -> 1 and cos(x + h/2) -> cos x, so the limit is cos x. Boxed d/dx (sin x) = cos x (printed key p533: cos x).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q2; book p532-534 = PDF p559-561; key book p533-534

questions.knowledgeNote: d/dx sqrt(u) = u'/(2 sqrt u) with u = 2x+3 gives 2/(2 sqrt(2x+3)) = 1/sqrt(2x+3). Geometric meaning: slope of the tangent.
questions.question: Q3. Define the differential coefficient of a function f(x) at a point and interpret it geometrically. Find from first principles the derivative of sqrt(2x + 3) with respect to x. (T.U. 2053)
questions.solution: Definition and geometry. f'(a) = lim(h->0) [f(a+h) - f(a)]/h. Geometrically the quotient is the slope of the chord joining P(a, f(a)) to Q(a+h, f(a+h)); as h -> 0 the chord turns into the tangent at P, so f'(a) is the slope of the tangent to y = f(x) at x = a, i.e. f'(a) = tan(psi) where psi is the angle the tangent makes with the positive x-axis. Step 1. f(x+h) - f(x) = sqrt(2x + 2h + 3) - sqrt(2x + 3) = [(2x + 2h + 3) - (2x + 3)]/[sqrt(2x + 2h + 3) + sqrt(2x + 3)] = 2h/[sqrt(2x + 2h + 3) + sqrt(2x + 3)]. Step 2. Divide by h: quotient = 2/[sqrt(2x + 2h + 3) + sqrt(2x + 3)]. Step 3. h -> 0: limit = 2/[2 sqrt(2x + 3)] = 1/sqrt(2x + 3). Boxed d/dx sqrt(2x + 3) = 1/sqrt(2x + 3), x > -3/2 (printed key p533: 1/sqrt(2x + 3)).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q3; book p532-534 = PDF p559-561; key book p533-534

questions.knowledgeNote: Same surd rationalisation as Q1 with the shift +1: derivative of sqrt(x+1) is 1/(2 sqrt(x+1)).
questions.question: Q4(i). Find from first principles the derivative of x + sqrt(x + 1). (T.U. 2051 H)
questions.solution: Step 1. f(x+h) - f(x) = h + [sqrt(x + 1 + h) - sqrt(x + 1)]. Step 2. Rationalise: sqrt(x + 1 + h) - sqrt(x + 1) = h/[sqrt(x + 1 + h) + sqrt(x + 1)]. Step 3. Divide by h: quotient = 1 + 1/[sqrt(x + 1 + h) + sqrt(x + 1)]. Step 4. h -> 0: derivative = 1 + 1/(2 sqrt(x + 1)). Boxed 1 + 1/(2 sqrt(x + 1)), x > -1 (printed key p533: 1 + 1/(2 sqrt(x+1))).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q4(i); book p532-534 = PDF p559-561; key book p533-534

questions.knowledgeNote: General surd rule by first principles: d/dx sqrt(ax+b) = a/(2 sqrt(ax+b)); dy/dx is the tangent gradient tan(theta).
questions.question: Q4(ii). Find from first principles the derivative of sqrt(ax + b) and define dy/dx as a slope. (T.U. 2052 H)
questions.solution: Step 1. f(x+h) - f(x) = sqrt(ax + ah + b) - sqrt(ax + b) = [(ax + ah + b) - (ax + b)]/[sqrt(ax + ah + b) + sqrt(ax + b)] = ah/[sqrt(ax + ah + b) + sqrt(ax + b)]. Step 2. Divide by h: quotient = a/[sqrt(ax + ah + b) + sqrt(ax + b)]. Step 3. h -> 0: derivative = a/[2 sqrt(ax + b)]. Boxed d/dx sqrt(ax + b) = a/(2 sqrt(ax + b)), ax + b > 0 (printed key p533: a/(2 sqrt(ax+b))). dy/dx as a slope. For the curve y = f(x), dy/dx at a point is the gradient of the tangent there: dy/dx = tan(theta) = rise/run measured along the tangent; a positive value means the curve rises, a negative value means it falls, and dy/dx = 0 marks a horizontal tangent (stationary point).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q4(ii); book p532-534 = PDF p559-561; key book p533-534

questions.knowledgeNote: Write the difference quotient of f+g as the sum of the two difference quotients and take limits term by term.
questions.question: Q5(i). Define the derivative of a function at any point. Prove that d/dx [f(x) + g(x)] = d/dx f(x) + d/dx g(x). (T.U. 2054)
questions.solution: Definition. If f is defined on an interval containing x, then f'(x) = lim(h->0) [f(x+h) - f(x)]/h whenever the limit exists; the function x -> f'(x) so obtained is the derivative of f. Proof (sum rule). Let y = f(x) + g(x). Then [y(x+h) - y(x)]/h = {[f(x+h) - f(x)] + [g(x+h) - g(x)]}/h = [f(x+h) - f(x)]/h + [g(x+h) - g(x)]/h. Because the limit of a sum is the sum of the limits (both exist by hypothesis), letting h -> 0 gives y' = f'(x) + g'(x). Boxed d/dx[f + g] = f' + g'. (The printed key carries this as a proof, p533.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q5(i); book p532-534 = PDF p559-561; key book p533-534

questions.knowledgeNote: The standard trick: insert f(x+h)g(x) - f(x+h)g(x) so that both difference quotients appear; the leftover f(x+h) -> f(x).
questions.question: Q5(ii). Prove that d/dx [f(x) g(x)] = f(x) d/dx g(x) + g(x) d/dx f(x). (T.U. 2054)
questions.solution: Proof (product rule). Let y = f(x) g(x). The difference quotient is [f(x+h)g(x+h) - f(x)g(x)]/h. Add and subtract f(x+h) g(x): = [f(x+h)g(x+h) - f(x+h)g(x) + f(x+h)g(x) - f(x)g(x)]/h = f(x+h)[g(x+h) - g(x)]/h + g(x)[f(x+h) - f(x)]/h. As h -> 0, f(x+h) -> f(x) (f is differentiable, hence continuous) and the two brackets tend to g'(x) and f'(x). Hence y' = f(x) g'(x) + g(x) f'(x). Boxed (the printed key carries this as a proof, p533).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q5(ii); book p532-534 = PDF p559-561; key book p533-534

questions.knowledgeNote: Binomial expansion of (t + 2h)^5; after dividing by h every surviving term beyond the first still carries h.
questions.question: Q6(i). Find from first principles the derivative of (2x + 3)^5.
questions.solution: Put t = 2x + 3, so the increment of t is 2h. Then [(t + 2h)^5 - t^5]/h = [5t^4(2h) + 10t^3(2h)^2 + 10t^2(2h)^3 + 5t(2h)^4 + (2h)^5]/h = 10t^4 + 40t^3 h + 80t^2 h^2 + 80t h^3 + 32h^4. Let h -> 0: derivative = 10t^4 = 10(2x + 3)^4. Boxed (printed key p533: 10(2x+3)^4).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q6(i); book p532-534 = PDF p559-561; key book p533-534

questions.knowledgeNote: cos P - cos Q = -2 sin((P+Q)/2) sin((P-Q)/2); the inner factor contributes the chain-rule a.
questions.question: Q6(iii). Find from first principles the derivative of cos(ax + b).
questions.solution: cos(ax + ah + b) - cos(ax + b) = -2 sin(ax + b + ah/2) sin(ah/2) (sum-to-product). Divide by h: quotient = -sin(ax + b + ah/2) * [sin(ah/2)/(h/2)] * a. As h -> 0, sin(ah/2)/(ah/2) -> 1 and the first factor -> sin(ax + b), so the derivative is -a sin(ax + b). Boxed (printed key p533: -a sin(ax+b)).

questions.knowledgeNote: Factor out 5^x; (a^h - 1)/h -> log_e a gives 5^x log_e 5.
questions.question: Q6(iv). Find from first principles the derivative of 5^x.
questions.solution: [5^(x+h) - 5^x]/h = 5^x (5^h - 1)/h. Use the standard limit lim(h->0)(a^h - 1)/h = log_e a: the derivative is 5^x log_e 5. Boxed (printed key p534: 5^x log_e 5).

questions.question: Q7(iv). Find dy/dx when sqrt(x) + sqrt(y) = sqrt(a).
questions.solution: Differentiate: 1/(2 sqrt x) + (1/(2 sqrt y)) y' = 0, so y' = -sqrt(y)/sqrt(x) = -sqrt(y/x). Boxed (printed key p534: -y^(1/2)/x^(1/2)).

questions.knowledgeNote: Logarithmic differentiation cancels the common factor (4y - 3x); the answer collapses to y/x.
questions.question: Q7(v). Find dy/dx when x^2 y^3 = (x + 2y)^5.
questions.solution: Take logs: 2 log x + 3 log y = 5 log(x + 2y). Differentiate: 2/x + 3y'/y = 5(1 + 2y')/(x + 2y). Collect y': y'[10/(x + 2y) - 3/y] = 2/x - 5/(x + 2y). Left bracket = [10y - 3(x + 2y)]/[y(x + 2y)] = (4y - 3x)/[y(x + 2y)]; right side = [2(x + 2y) - 5x]/[x(x + 2y)] = (4y - 3x)/[x(x + 2y)]. Hence y' = y/x (for 4y != 3x). Boxed y/x (printed key p534: y/x).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q7(v); book p532-534 = PDF p559-561; key book p533-534

questions.knowledgeNote: The x^2 cancels the -1/x^2 of the inner derivative, leaving -cos(1/x) + 2x sin(1/x).
questions.question: Q7(vi). Find dy/dx when y = x^2 sin(1/x).
questions.solution: Product + chain rule: y' = 2x sin(1/x) + x^2 cos(1/x)(-1/x^2) = 2x sin(1/x) - cos(1/x). Boxed (printed key p534: -cos(1/x) + 2x sin(1/x)).

questions.knowledgeNote: 1 - (3x-4x^3)^2 factors as (1-x^2)(1-4x^2)^2; the modulus gives +-3/sqrt(1-x^2), i.e. 3/sqrt(1-x^2) on the branch |x| < 1/2.
questions.question: Q7(vii). Find dy/dx when y = sin^-1(3x - 4x^3). (T.U. 2048)
questions.solution: y' = 3(1 - 4x^2)/sqrt(1 - (3x - 4x^3)^2). Now 1 - (3x - 4x^3)^2 = 1 - 9x^2 + 24x^4 - 16x^6 = (1 - x^2)(1 - 4x^2)^2, so y' = 3(1 - 4x^2)/[|1 - 4x^2| sqrt(1 - x^2)] = 3/sqrt(1 - x^2) when |x| < 1/2. Boxed 3/sqrt(1 - x^2) (printed key p534: 3/sqrt(1-x^2)); for 1/2 < |x| < 1 the derivative is -3/sqrt(1 - x^2) because |1 - 4x^2| = -(1 - 4x^2) there. The printing states the |x| < 1/2 branch, on which 3x - 4x^3 = sin 3(theta) with x = sin theta; no book error, only the branch qualifier added.

questions.question: Q7(ix). Find dy/dx when x = a(theta - sin theta), y = a(1 - cos theta).
questions.solution: dx/dtheta = a(1 - cos theta), dy/dtheta = a sin theta. dy/dx = sin theta/(1 - cos theta) = [2 sin(theta/2)cos(theta/2)]/[2 sin^2(theta/2)] = cot(theta/2). Boxed (printed key p534: cot(theta/2)).

questions.knowledgeNote: Three-factor logarithmic differentiation: each factor contributes its exponent times (inner derivative)/(factor).
questions.question: Q7(x). Find dy/dx when y = x^2 sqrt(2x + 3) / cbrt(4x + 1).
questions.solution: Take logs: log y = 2 log x + (1/2)log(2x + 3) - (1/3)log(4x + 1). Differentiate: y'/y = 2/x + 1/(2x + 3) - 4/[3(4x + 1)]. Hence y' = y[2/x + 1/(2x + 3) - 4/(3(4x + 1))]. Boxed (printed key p534: y[2/x + 1/(2x+3) - 4/(3(4x+1))]).

questions.knowledgeNote: f(0) fixes the intercept c, f'(0) fixes the gradient m; then evaluate at x = 2.
questions.question: Q8. If f(x) = mx + c and f(0) = f'(0) = 1, what is f(2)?
questions.solution: f(0) = c = 1. f'(x) = m for every x, so f'(0) = m = 1. Hence f(x) = x + 1 and f(2) = 3. Boxed 3 (printed key p534: 3).

questions.knowledgeNote: Implicit differentiation, then replace x by sin y/sin(a+y); the bracket collapses to sin a/sin(a+y).
questions.question: Q10(a). If sin y = x sin(a + y), prove that dy/dx = sin^2(a + y)/sin a.
questions.solution: Differentiate implicitly with respect to x: cos y * y' = sin(a + y) + x cos(a + y) * y'. Collect y': y'[cos y - x cos(a + y)] = sin(a + y). Eliminate x using the given relation x = sin y/sin(a + y): cos y - x cos(a + y) = [cos y sin(a + y) - sin y cos(a + y)]/sin(a + y) = sin[(a + y) - y]/sin(a + y) = sin a/sin(a + y). Therefore y' = sin(a + y) * sin(a + y)/sin a = sin^2(a + y)/sin a. Boxed (printed key, book p534).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q10(a); book p533-534 = PDF p560-561; key book p534 = PDF p561

questions.knowledgeNote: Same pattern as Q10(a): the difference formula cos y cos T + sin y sin T = cos(T - y) is the whole proof.
questions.question: Q10(b). If sin y = x cos(a + y), show that dy/dx = cos^2(a + y)/cos a.
questions.solution: Differentiate: cos y * y' = cos(a + y) - x sin(a + y) * y', so y'[cos y + x sin(a + y)] = cos(a + y). With x = sin y/cos(a + y): cos y + x sin(a + y) = [cos y cos(a + y) + sin y sin(a + y)]/cos(a + y) = cos[(a + y) - y]/cos(a + y) = cos a/cos(a + y). Hence y' = cos(a + y) * cos(a + y)/cos a = cos^2(a + y)/cos a. Boxed (printed key, book p534).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q10(b); book p533-534 = PDF p560-561; key book p534 = PDF p561

questions.knowledgeNote: Squaring makes the quotient differentiation trivial; the identity (1-x)^2 y^2 = 1-x^2 converts the result to y/(1-x^2).
questions.question: Q11. If y = sqrt((1 + x)/(1 - x)), prove that dy/dx = y/(1 - x^2).
questions.solution: Square: y^2 = (1 + x)/(1 - x). Differentiate implicitly: 2y y' = [(1 - x) + (1 + x)]/(1 - x)^2 = 2/(1 - x)^2, so y' = 1/[(1 - x)^2 y]. Now (1 - x)^2 y^2 = (1 - x)(1 + x) = 1 - x^2, hence (1 - x)^2 y = (1 - x^2)/y and y' = y/(1 - x^2). Boxed (printed key, book p534).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q11; book p533-534 = PDF p560-561; key book p534 = PDF p561

questions.knowledgeNote: Variable base and variable exponent (x^sin x): take logs first, then y' = y[v' log u + v u'/u].
questions.question: Q12(i). Find the derivative of x^(sin x).
questions.solution: Logarithmic differentiation: log y = sin x * log x, so y'/y = cos x log x + sin x/x. Hence y' = x^(sin x)(sin x/x + cos x log x). Boxed (printed key p534: x^(sin x)((sin x)/x + cos x log x)).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q12(i); book p533-534 = PDF p560-561; key book p534 = PDF p561

questions.knowledgeNote: (sin x)^x: the bracket is log u + x u'/u = log sin x + x cot x.
questions.question: Q12(ii). Find the derivative of (sin x)^x.
questions.solution: log y = x log(sin x), so y'/y = log(sin x) + x cot x. Hence y' = (sin x)^x (x cot x + log sin x). Boxed (printed key p534).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q12(ii); book p533-534 = PDF p560-561; key book p534 = PDF p561

questions.knowledgeNote: Product of two logs: differentiate log x and log sin x separately, each against the other factor.
questions.question: Q12(iii). Find the derivative of (sin x)^(log x).
questions.solution: log y = log x * log(sin x), so y'/y = (1/x)log(sin x) + log x * cot x. Hence y' = (sin x)^(log x) [(1/x)log sin x + cot x log x]. Boxed (printed key p534).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q12(iii); book p533-534 = PDF p560-561; key book p534 = PDF p561

questions.knowledgeNote: Tower e^(x^x): differentiate the inner tower x^x logarithmically, then apply the outer chain rule.
questions.question: Q12(iv). Find the derivative of e^(x^x).
questions.solution: Let u = x^x. Then log u = x log x and u' = x^x(1 + log x). Chain rule: y' = e^(x^x) * u' = e^(x^x) * x^x(1 + log x). Boxed (printed key p534: e^(x^x).x^x(1 + log x)).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q12(iv); book p533-534 = PDF p560-561; key book p534 = PDF p561

questions.knowledgeNote: x^(e^x): product rule on e^x log x gives e^x(log x + 1/x).
questions.question: Q12(v). Find the derivative of x^(e^x).
questions.solution: log y = e^x log x, so y'/y = e^x log x + e^x/x = e^x(log x + 1/x). Hence y' = x^(e^x) e^x(log x + 1/x). Boxed (printed key p534).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q12(v); book p533-534 = PDF p560-561; key book p534 = PDF p561

questions.knowledgeNote: Nested log: d/dx log(log x) = 1/(x log x) supplies the second term.
questions.question: Q12(vi). Find the derivative of (log x)^(tan x).
questions.solution: log y = tan x * log(log x), so y'/y = sec^2 x log(log x) + tan x * 1/(x log x). Hence y' = (log x)^(tan x){sec^2 x log(log x) + tan x/(x log x)}. Boxed (printed key p534).

questions.knowledgeNote: (tan x)^(log x): the u'/u part is sec^2 x/tan x, which multiplies log x.
questions.question: Q12(vii). Find the derivative of (tan x)^(log x). (T.U. 2048 H)
questions.solution: log y = log x * log(tan x), so y'/y = (1/x)log(tan x) + log x * sec^2 x/tan x. Hence y' = (tan x)^(log x){(1/x)log tan x + (sec^2 x/tan x)log x}. Boxed (printed key p534).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q12(vii); book p533-534 = PDF p560-561; key book p534 = PDF p561

questions.knowledgeNote: x^(sec x): sec x differentiates to sec x tan x, and sec x/x survives from the log x term.
questions.question: Q12(viii). Find the derivative of x^(sec x).
questions.solution: log y = sec x * log x, so y'/y = sec x tan x log x + sec x/x = sec x(tan x log x + 1/x). Hence y' = x^(sec x) sec x(tan x log x + 1/x). Boxed (printed key p534).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q12(viii); book p533-534 = PDF p560-561; key book p534 = PDF p561

questions.knowledgeNote: (sin x)^(cos x): the derivative of cos x is -sin x, which is why the log term is subtracted.
questions.question: Q12(ix). Find the derivative of (sin x)^(cos x). (T.U. 2053)
questions.solution: log y = cos x * log(sin x), so y'/y = -sin x log(sin x) + cos x * cot x. Hence y' = (sin x)^(cos x){cos x cot x - sin x log(sin x)}. Boxed (printed key p534).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q12(ix); book p533-534 = PDF p560-561; key book p534 = PDF p561

questions.knowledgeNote: y = x^y: differentiate the base and the exponent separately, then use x^y = y to simplify y.x^(y-1) to y^2/x.
questions.question: Q13(i). Find dy/dx when y = x^y.
questions.solution: Differentiate with respect to x, treating the exponent as a variable: dy/dx = y x^(y-1) + x^y log x * dy/dx (product rule on x^y). So y'[1 - x^y log x] = y x^(y-1). Using x^y = y: y x^(y-1) = y * y/x = y^2/x, hence y' = (y^2/x)/(1 - y log x) = y^2/[x(1 - y log x)]. Boxed (printed key p534).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q13(i); book p533-534 = PDF p560-561; key book p534 = PDF p561

questions.knowledgeNote: The product of two powers becomes a sum of logs; the implicit derivative then collects y' against (log x + x/y).
questions.question: Q13(ii). Find dy/dx when x^y . y^x = 1. (T.U. 2051 H)
questions.solution: Take logs: y log x + x log y = 0. Differentiate: y' log x + y/x + log y + x y'/y = 0, so y'(log x + x/y) = -(y/x + log y). Hence y' = -(y/x + log y)/(log x + x/y) = -y(y + x log y)/[x(y log x + x)]. Boxed (printed key p534).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q13(ii); book p533-534 = PDF p560-561; key book p534 = PDF p561

questions.knowledgeNote: Homogeneous-type relation: the common factor (my - nx) cancels, leaving the symmetric answer y/x.
questions.question: Q13(iii). Find dy/dx when x^m y^n = (x + y)^(m+n).
questions.solution: Take logs: m log x + n log y = (m + n)log(x + y). Differentiate: m/x + n y'/y = (m + n)(1 + y')/(x + y). Collect y': y'[(m + n)/(x + y) - n/y] = m/x - (m + n)/(x + y). Left bracket = [(m + n)y - n(x + y)]/[y(x + y)] = (my - nx)/[y(x + y)]; right side = [m(x + y) - (m + n)x]/[x(x + y)] = (my - nx)/[x(x + y)]. Hence y' = y/x (for my != nx). Boxed y/x (printed key p534).

questions.knowledgeNote: Each exponential contributes its chain factor: cos x on the left, cos y on the right.
questions.question: Q13(iv). Find dy/dx when e^(sin x) + e^(sin y) = 1.
questions.solution: Differentiate: e^(sin x) cos x + e^(sin y) cos y * y' = 0, so y' = -e^(sin x) cos x / (e^(sin y) cos y). Boxed (printed key p534).

questions.knowledgeNote: x^y = y^x is the classic log case; collect y' against (log x - x/y).
questions.question: Q13(v). Find dy/dx when x^y = y^x. (T.U. 2048)
questions.solution: Take logs: y log x = x log y. Differentiate: y' log x + y/x = log y + x y'/y, so y'(log x - x/y) = log y - y/x. Hence y' = (log y - y/x)/(log x - x/y) = y(x log y - y)/[x(y log x - x)]. Boxed (printed key p534).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.17 Additional Questions (Derivative) Q13(v); book p533-534 = PDF p560-561; key book p534 = PDF p561

questions.knowledgeNote: Symmetry: the same expression appears on each side; the missing x^(sin x)/y^(sin y) factor is 1 by the hypothesis.
questions.question: Q13(vi). Find dy/dx when x^(sin x) = y^(sin y). (T.U. 2049)
questions.solution: Take logs: sin x log x = sin y log y. Differentiate both sides with respect to x: cos x log x + sin x/x = [cos y log y + sin y/y] * y'. Hence y' = [cos x log x + sin x/x]/[cos y log y + sin y/y] = y(x cos x log x + sin x)/[x(y cos y log y + sin y)]. Boxed (printed key p534). Note: the full implicit form carries the factor x^(sin x)/y^(sin y), which equals 1 by the given equation — that is why the key has no such factor.
